To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the predominant sense of a word is highly dependent on the topic domain of the text, that the topic domain of a text can be determined by text categorization and that this information can be used to improve WSD.

the sense of a word in a document can be predicted with reasonable accuracy by estimating the sense prior from a domain-specific document corpus, that the accuracy is higher than the accuracy of sense estimation from a domain-independent corpus, and that the accuracy is comparable to that of a supervised system trained on a manually annotated corpus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (a) Can the topic of a text be automatically determined and used to estimate sense priors?
the following questions:  • How can we automatically determine the predominant sense of words in a given domain?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a text categorizer can be beneficial for the task of WSD.
the best results were obtained when the sense distributions of words were estimated from corpora that are both sense-annotated and domain-specific.
the domain information is useful for word sense disambigu-ation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the topic of a document is an important feature for WSD, but the domain of a document is not a good proxy for the topic.
we have developed a method for unsupervised estimation that outperforms previous methods for a large set of polysemous words.
we can estimate word senses from a large domain independent corpus and then use the estimated word senses for a particular domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the domain of a corpus can be estimated from the text itself and that the domain of the text can be used for improved estimation of the predominant senses of words.
it is possible to improve sense estimates using domain information, even when this information is not available in the form of manually sense-annotatd corpora.
the predominant sense of a word in a given document is not only influenced by the document's domain, but also by its genre.
